questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सर्वाधिक क्षारकीय है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is most basic ?
questions.solution: MnO is the most basic among the given manganese oxides because Mn is in the lowest oxidation state (+2) in MnO. As the oxidation state of Mn increases, the oxides become progressively less basic and more acidic. MnO₂ (+4) is amphoteric, Mn₂O₃ (+3) is weakly basic, and Mn₂O₇ (+7) is acidic in nature. Therefore, MnO with the lowest oxidation state of manganese is the most basic.

questions.text: निम्न में से कौन सा वक्र प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया को निरूपित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?

options.A: Graph of t½ vs [R]₀ showing a straight line with positive slope
options.B: Graph of t½ vs [R]₀ showing a horizontal straight line (constant t½)
options.C: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a horizontal straight line
options.D: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a curve decreasing then levelling

options_english.A: Graph of t½ vs [R]₀ showing a straight line with positive slope
options_english.B: Graph of t½ vs [R]₀ showing a horizontal straight line (constant t½)
options_english.C: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a horizontal straight line
options_english.D: Graph of Rate vs Concentration showing a curve decreasing then levelling

questions.solution: For a first-order reaction, the half-life (t½ = 0.693/k) is independent of the initial concentration [R]₀. Therefore, a graph of t½ versus [R]₀ would be a horizontal straight line, as shown in option B. Option A is incorrect because it shows t½ increasing with [R]₀, which is characteristic of a zero-order reaction. Options C and D represent rate vs concentration plots, which are not characteristic graphs for identifying first-order kinetics through t½.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित विलयनों में से किसका उच्चतम परासरण दाब होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following solutions will have the highest osmotic pressure ?
questions.solution: Osmotic pressure (π = iCRT) depends on the van't Hoff factor i. CaCl₂ dissociates into 3 ions (Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻), giving i = 3, so effective concentration = 0.3 M. KCl dissociates into 2 ions (K⁺ + Cl⁻), giving i = 2, effective concentration = 0.2 M. Glucose and urea are non-electrolytes with i = 1, effective concentration = 0.1 M each. Since 0.1 M CaCl₂ produces the highest number of solute particles, it has the highest osmotic pressure.

questions.text: अभिक्रिया : N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ के लिए, NH₃ के प्रति अभिक्रिया वेग है
questions.text_english: For a reaction : N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, the rate of reaction with respect to NH₃ is
questions.solution: For the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, the rate is expressed as: Rate = -Δ[N₂]/Δt = -1/3 Δ[H₂]/Δt = +1/2 Δ[NH₃]/Δt. Since NH₃ is a product, its concentration increases with time, so the sign is positive. The stoichiometric coefficient of NH₃ is 2, so the rate with respect to NH₃ is +1/2 Δ[NH₃]/Δt. Option B is wrong because the sign should be positive for a product. Options A and C use incorrect stoichiometric coefficients.

questions.text: अम्लीय माध्यम में Cr₂O₇²⁻ के 1 मोल को Cr³⁺ में अपचयित करने के लिए कितने फैराडे की आवश्यकता होगी ?
questions.text_english: How many Faradays are required to reduce 1 mol of Cr₂O₇²⁻ to Cr³⁺ in acidic medium ?
questions.solution: In Cr₂O₇²⁻, each Cr is in +6 oxidation state. When reduced to Cr³⁺, each Cr gains 3 electrons. Since one mole of Cr₂O₇²⁻ contains 2 moles of Cr atoms, the total electrons required = 2 × 3 = 6 electrons per formula unit. Therefore, 6 Faradays are required to reduce 1 mole of Cr₂O₇²⁻ to Cr³⁺ in acidic medium.

questions.text_english: Which of the following Grignard Reagent will be used to prepare cyclohexylmethanol (cyclohexane with CH₂OH group) when treated with methanal ?

options.B: Cyclohexyl-CH₂MgBr (benzylmagnesium bromide type with cyclohexane ring)

questions.solution: To prepare cyclohexylmethanol (cyclohexane-CH₂OH) from methanal (HCHO), we need a Grignard reagent whose carbon adds to the carbonyl carbon of HCHO and after hydrolysis gives a -CH₂OH group. The Grignard reagent reacts as: R-MgBr + HCHO → R-CH₂OH. Here R must be the cyclohexyl group, so cyclohexyl-MgBr (option C) is the correct Grignard reagent. Other options would give different carbon chain lengths.

questions.text: [Pt(en)₂Cl₂]²⁺ में Pt की द्वितीयक संयोजकता है
questions.text_english: The secondary valency of Pt in [Pt(en)₂Cl₂]²⁺ is
questions.solution: Secondary valency (coordination number) of the central metal ion is the total number of ligand donor atoms bonded to it. In [Pt(en)₂Cl₂]²⁺, 'en' (ethylenediamine) is a bidentate ligand donating 2 donor atoms each. Two 'en' ligands donate 2 × 2 = 4 donor atoms. Two Cl⁻ ligands donate 2 × 1 = 2 donor atoms. Total coordination number = 4 + 2 = 6. Therefore, the secondary valency of Pt is 6.

questions.text: (CH₃)₃C – OC₂H₅, HI के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है
questions.text_english: (CH₃)₃C – OC₂H₅ on reaction with HI gives
questions.solution: When an unsymmetrical ether like (CH₃)₃C–OC₂H₅ reacts with HI, the cleavage occurs via an SN1 mechanism at the more substituted (tertiary) carbon. The iodide ion attacks the tertiary carbocation formed from (CH₃)₃C⁺, yielding (CH₃)₃C–I. The ethoxy part leaves as C₂H₅–O⁻ which picks up H⁺ to give C₂H₅–OH. Thus the products are (CH₃)₃C–OH... wait — the tertiary carbon gets the iodide: products are (CH₃)₃C–I and C₂H₅–OH... but the standard answer for this type is (CH₃)₃COH + C₂H₅I via SN2 on the less hindered primary carbon. With HI and a tertiary ether, I⁻ attacks the less hindered primary ethyl carbon (SN2), giving C₂H₅I and the tertiary alcohol (CH₃)₃COH. Therefore option B is correct.

questions.text: ऐनिलीन सीधे नाइट्रोकरण से देता है
questions.text_english: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: The –NH₂ group in aniline is a strong ortho/para director. In strongly acidic nitration conditions, some aniline gets protonated to form anilinium ion which is a meta director, but predominantly the free aniline undergoes ortho/para direction. The product distribution from direct nitration of aniline is approximately 51% ortho-nitroaniline, 47% para-nitroaniline, and only 2% meta-nitroaniline. This confirms that –NH₂ strongly activates ortho and para positions, giving option A as correct.

questions.text_english: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers ?

options.A: They have the same chemical reactivity.
options.B: They have the same specific rotation.
options.C: They have the same melting or boiling point.
options.D: They have the same refractive index.

options_english.A: They have the same chemical reactivity.
options_english.B: They have the same specific rotation.
options_english.C: They have the same melting or boiling point.
options_english.D: They have the same refractive index.

questions.solution: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. They share identical physical properties such as melting point, boiling point, refractive index, and density. They also show the same chemical reactivity in achiral environments. However, the one property that differs between enantiomers is the direction of rotation of plane-polarised light: one rotates it clockwise (+) and the other rotates it counterclockwise (–) by equal magnitudes. Therefore, they do NOT have the same specific rotation. Option B is the statement that is not true.

questions.text: अनपचयी शर्करा का उदाहरण है
questions.text_english: An example of non-reducing sugar is
questions.solution: A reducing sugar is one that can act as a reducing agent due to the presence of a free aldehyde or ketone group (or a hemiacetal/hemiketal form). Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because both its glucose and fructose units are linked through their anomeric carbon atoms (C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose), leaving no free anomeric –OH group. Glucose, lactose, and maltose all have free anomeric hydroxyl groups and can open to the aldehyde form, making them reducing sugars. Hence sucrose is the correct answer.

questions.text: बेन्जीन डाइएज़ोनियम क्लोराइड दुर्बल क्षारकीय माध्यम में फ़ीनॉल के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है
questions.text_english: Benzene diazonium chloride on reaction with phenol in weakly basic medium gives
questions.solution: When benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol in weakly basic medium, a coupling reaction occurs. Phenol in basic medium forms phenoxide ion (C₆H₅O⁻), which is a more activated aromatic compound. The electrophilic diazonium ion (C₆H₅N₂⁺) attacks the highly activated para position of phenoxide to give p-hydroxyazobenzene (an azo dye). This is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction known as diazo coupling, and option D is correct.

In DNA, the two strands are complementary to each other, meaning Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T) and Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C). The formation of hydrogen bonds between specific base pairs (Reason R) is the direct cause of the complementarity of the two strands (Assertion A).

questions.text: एथेनॉल और ऐसीटोन मिश्रण द्वारा राउल्ट नियम से किस प्रकार का विचलन दर्शाया जाता है ? कारण दीजिए । एथेनॉल और ऐसीटोन को मिलाने पर बने विलयन के क्वथनांक का क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english: What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by mixture of ethanol and acetone ? Give reason. What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing ethanol and acetone ?

key_points: Positive deviation from Raoult's law
Reason: Ethanol molecules have H-bonding among themselves; in mixture, acetone-ethanol interactions are weaker than pure component interactions, so vapour pressure increases
Boiling point decreases (solution is more volatile than pure components)

questions.solution: The mixture of ethanol and acetone shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. In pure ethanol, strong hydrogen bonds exist between ethanol molecules. When acetone is added, the acetone-ethanol interactions are weaker (only dipole-dipole) than the original ethanol-ethanol hydrogen bonding. This weakening causes each component to escape into the vapour phase more easily, increasing the total vapour pressure above the ideal value predicted by Raoult's law. As vapour pressure increases, the boiling point of the solution decreases compared to the pure components.

sub_questions.solution: Add AgNO₃ solution to aqueous solutions of each compound. [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl has Cl⁻ as free ion outside the coordination sphere, so it gives a white precipitate of AgCl immediately. [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ has Cl⁻ inside the coordination sphere, so it does NOT give a precipitate with AgNO₃. Alternatively, BaCl₂ test: [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ (free SO₄²⁻) gives white BaSO₄ precipitate; [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl does not.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by the 'Chelate effect'? Give an example.

key_points: Chelate effect: polydentate ligands form more stable complexes than monodentate ligands due to increased entropy
Example: [Co(en)₃]³⁺ more stable than [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺

sub_questions.solution: The chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of complexes formed by polydentate (chelating) ligands compared to analogous complexes with monodentate ligands. This extra stability arises due to a favourable entropy change when a chelating ligand replaces multiple monodentate ligands, as the number of free particles in solution increases. For example, [Co(en)₃]³⁺ (with three bidentate ethylenediamine ligands) is significantly more stable than [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺.

questions.solution: Part (a): (i) Diamminesilver(I) dicyanoargentate(I); (ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III). Part (b): (i) Add AgNO₃ to aqueous solutions: [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl gives white AgCl precipitate (free Cl⁻ outside sphere), while [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ does not. (ii) Chelate effect is the extra stability of complexes with polydentate ligands due to entropy gain; example: [Co(en)₃]³⁺ is more stable than [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺.

questions.text: हैलोऐरीनें नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति कम अभिक्रियाशील क्यों होते हैं ? दो कारण दीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.

key_points: Resonance stabilisation: lone pair of halogen delocalises into the ring, making C–X bond have partial double bond character, which is stronger and shorter than in haloalkanes
sp² hybridised carbon: the carbon bearing the halogen is sp² hybridised, making it less susceptible to nucleophilic attack due to higher s-character and less positive charge

questions.solution: Haloarenes are less reactive toward nucleophilic substitution for two main reasons. First, in haloarenes the halogen atom donates its lone pair into the aromatic π system through resonance, giving the C–X bond a partial double bond character. This makes the bond shorter and stronger than a typical C–X bond in haloalkanes, making it harder to break. Second, the carbon bonded to the halogen is sp² hybridised, which means the orbital used for the C–X bond has more s-character, holding the electrons more tightly and making the carbon less electrophilic and less susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया एक चरण में सम्पन्न होती है : 2A + B → 2C

questions.text_english: Following reaction takes place in one step: 2A + B → 2C. How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?

key_points: Rate = k[A]²[B]; when volume decreases to 1/3, concentrations become 3 times each
New rate = k(3[A])²(3[B]) = 27k[A]²[B] = 27 times original rate
Order of reaction does not change; it remains 3 (third order)

questions.solution: Since the reaction 2A + B → 2C occurs in one step, its rate law is Rate = k[A]²[B], making it third order overall. When the volume is decreased to one-third, all concentrations triple: [A] becomes 3[A] and [B] becomes 3[B]. New rate = k(3[A])²(3[B]) = k × 9[A]² × 3[B] = 27k[A]²[B]. Therefore, the rate increases 27 times. The order of reaction remains unchanged at 3, because order depends on the mechanism of the reaction, not on concentrations.

sub_questions.text_english: Acidic amino acids and basic amino acids

key_points: Acidic amino acids have more –COOH groups than –NH₂ groups (e.g. aspartic acid); basic amino acids have more –NH₂ groups than –COOH groups (e.g. lysine)

sub_questions.solution: Acidic amino acids contain more carboxyl (–COOH) groups than amino (–NH₂) groups, so their aqueous solutions are acidic; example: aspartic acid. Basic amino acids contain more amino (–NH₂) groups than carboxyl (–COOH) groups, so their aqueous solutions are basic; example: lysine.

sub_questions.text: न्यूक्लिओटाइड और न्यूक्लियोसाइड
sub_questions.text_english: Nucleotide and Nucleoside

key_points: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar; Nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group

sub_questions.solution: A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) linked to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) by an N-glycosidic bond. A nucleotide is a nucleoside with one or more phosphate groups esterified to the sugar. In other words, nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group. Nucleotides are the monomeric units of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), while nucleosides lack the phosphate group.

questions.solution: (i) Acidic amino acids have more –COOH than –NH₂ groups (e.g. aspartic acid); basic amino acids have more –NH₂ than –COOH groups (e.g. lysine). (ii) A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base + pentose sugar; a nucleotide is a nucleoside + phosphate group. Nucleotides are the building blocks of DNA and RNA.

questions.text: C₄H₉Br आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X', जलीय KOH के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक ऐल्कोहॉल देता है । इस अभिक्रिया का वेग केवल यौगिक 'X' की सांद्रता पर निर्भर करता है । जब यौगिक 'X' के ध्रुवण घूर्णक समावयव 'Y' को जलीय KOH विलयन के साथ अभिक्रियित किया गया तो अभिक्रिया वेग यौगिक 'Y' की सांद्रता और जलीय KOH दोनों पर निर्भर पाया गया ।
questions.text_english: Compound 'X' with molecular formula C₄H₉Br reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' दोनों के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.

key_points: X: (CH₃)₃CBr (tert-butyl bromide)
Y: CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₃ (sec-butyl bromide, optically active)

sub_questions.solution: X reacts via SN1 (rate depends only on [X]), so X is a tertiary halide: (CH₃)₃CBr (2-bromo-2-methylpropane or tert-butyl bromide). Y is an optically active isomer of X with molecular formula C₄H₉Br that reacts via SN2 (rate depends on both [Y] and [KOH]): CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₃ (2-bromobutane or sec-butyl bromide), which has a chiral centre.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन रेसिमीकरण करेगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?

key_points: X undergoes racemisation via SN1 mechanism through planar carbocation intermediate

sub_questions.solution: X ((CH₃)₃CBr) will undergo racemisation because it reacts by the SN1 mechanism. In SN1, a planar carbocation intermediate is formed, which can be attacked by the nucleophile (OH⁻) from either face with equal probability. This produces a 50:50 mixture of enantiomers (racemic mixture). Y reacts by SN2, giving inversion of configuration, not racemisation.

sub_questions.text: 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन विन्यास के प्रतिलोमन के साथ उत्पाद बनाएगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?

key_points: Y undergoes inversion of configuration via SN2 mechanism (Walden inversion)

sub_questions.solution: Y (2-bromobutane, sec-butyl bromide) will form the product with inversion of configuration because it reacts by the SN2 mechanism. In SN2, the nucleophile OH⁻ attacks the chiral carbon from the back side (anti to the leaving group Br⁻) in a single concerted step. This back-side attack causes the Walden inversion, resulting in a product with configuration opposite to that of the starting material.

questions.solution: X is (CH₃)₃CBr (tert-butyl bromide), which reacts by SN1 (rate depends only on [X]). Y is CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₃ (2-bromobutane, sec-butyl bromide), an optically active isomer that reacts by SN2 (rate depends on both [Y] and [KOH]). X undergoes racemisation because its SN1 reaction proceeds through a planar carbocation, which can be attacked from either face. Y undergoes inversion of configuration (Walden inversion) because its SN2 reaction involves back-side attack by the nucleophile.

questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in the following: (a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction (b) Kolbe's reaction (c) Friedal-Crafts acylation of anisole

sub_questions.text: राइमर-टीमन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Reimer-Tiemann reaction

key_points: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH → salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)

sub_questions.solution: The Reimer-Tiemann reaction involves the treatment of phenol with chloroform (CHCl₃) in the presence of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to introduce an aldehyde group at the ortho position of the phenolic ring. The product is salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde): C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + 3NaOH → 2-HOC₆H₄CHO + 3NaCl + 2H₂O.

sub_questions.text: कोल्बे अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Kolbe's reaction

key_points: Sodium phenoxide + CO₂ (high pressure, 400 K) → sodium salicylate → H⁺ → salicylic acid

sub_questions.solution: Kolbe's reaction (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction) involves treating sodium phenoxide (C₆H₅ONa) with CO₂ under high pressure (at about 400 K). The CO₂ acts as an electrophile and attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ring to form sodium salicylate, which on acidification gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid): C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ → HOC₆H₄COONa → (H⁺) HOC₆H₄COOH.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिसोल की फ्रिडेल-क्राफ्ट ऐसिलन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Friedal-Crafts acylation of anisole

key_points: Anisole + CH₃COCl + AlCl₃ → para-methoxyacetophenone (major) + ortho-methoxyacetophenone (minor)

sub_questions.solution: In Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole, anisole reacts with acetyl chloride (CH₃COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ as a Lewis acid catalyst. The –OCH₃ group is an ortho/para director. The major product is para-methoxyacetophenone (4-methoxyacetophenone) due to steric reasons favouring para substitution, along with a minor amount of ortho-methoxyacetophenone: C₆H₅OCH₃ + CH₃COCl → (AlCl₃) p-CH₃O-C₆H₄-COCH₃ (major product).

questions.solution: (a) Reimer-Tiemann: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH → salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) + 3NaCl + 2H₂O. (b) Kolbe: Sodium phenoxide + CO₂ (high P, 400K) → sodium salicylate → H⁺ → salicylic acid. (c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole: anisole + CH₃COCl + AlCl₃ → p-methoxyacetophenone (major product) via electrophilic aromatic substitution at para position.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (a) कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक समतुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों से उच्च होते हैं । (b) ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है । (c) अमोनिया और इसके व्युत्पन्नों का कार्बोनिल समूह के साथ नाभिकरागी संयोजन प्रबल अम्लीय माध्यम में नहीं होता है ।
questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following: (a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses. (b) Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature. (c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

sub_questions.text: कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक समतुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों से उच्च होते हैं ।
sub_questions.text_english: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.

key_points: Carboxylic acids form dimers through two intermolecular hydrogen bonds, effectively doubling their molecular mass in the liquid state

sub_questions.solution: Carboxylic acids form stable dimers in the liquid state through two intermolecular hydrogen bonds between two –COOH groups. This effectively doubles the molecular mass of the species in solution, requiring more energy to break these stronger intermolecular associations. Alcohols form only one hydrogen bond per molecule. Therefore, carboxylic acids have significantly higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.

key_points: The α-carbon is adjacent to the electron-withdrawing C=O group; the carbanion formed after removal of α-H is stabilised by resonance (enolate ion)

sub_questions.solution: The α-hydrogen atoms (on the carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group) are acidic because the carbanion (enolate ion) formed after their removal is stabilised by resonance with the carbonyl group. The negative charge is delocalized between the α-carbon and the oxygen of the C=O group, making the enolate ion relatively stable. This resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base lowers the energy required to remove the α-H, making it acidic.

sub_questions.text: अमोनिया और इसके व्युत्पन्नों का कार्बोनिल समूह के साथ नाभिकरागी संयोजन प्रबल अम्लीय माध्यम में नहीं होता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

key_points: In strongly acidic medium, NH₃ and its derivatives get protonated (NH₄⁺), losing their nucleophilic lone pair and becoming unable to attack the carbonyl carbon

sub_questions.solution: Ammonia and its derivatives act as nucleophiles because of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom. In a strongly acidic medium, the nitrogen gets protonated (e.g., NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺), which uses up the lone pair. Without the lone pair, the nitrogen can no longer act as a nucleophile and cannot attack the carbonyl carbon. Therefore, nucleophilic addition does not occur in strongly acidic conditions.

questions.solution: (a) Carboxylic acids form dimers via two intermolecular H-bonds, effectively doubling their molecular weight in the liquid phase, hence higher boiling points than alcohols of similar mass. (b) α-Hydrogens are acidic because the enolate carbanion formed after their removal is stabilised by resonance with the C=O group. (c) In strongly acidic medium, NH₃ and derivatives get protonated (lose their lone pair), so they can no longer act as nucleophiles to attack the carbonyl carbon.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पदों को परिभाषित कीजिए : (a) ऐनोमर (b) प्रतीप शर्करा (c) ग्लाइकोसाइडी बंध
questions.text_english: Define the following terms: (a) Anomers (b) Invert sugar (c) Glycosidic linkage

sub_questions.text: ऐनोमर
sub_questions.text_english: Anomers

key_points: Anomers are cyclic stereoisomers of a monosaccharide differing only in configuration at the anomeric carbon (C1 in aldoses, C2 in ketoses); called α and β forms

sub_questions.solution: Anomers are a pair of diastereomers of a cyclic monosaccharide that differ from each other only in the configuration at the anomeric carbon (C-1 in aldoses or C-2 in ketoses). They are designated as α and β anomers. For example, α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose are anomers of each other, differing in the orientation of the –OH group at C-1.

sub_questions.text: प्रतीप शर्करा
sub_questions.text_english: Invert sugar

key_points: Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose obtained by hydrolysis of sucrose; sucrose is dextrorotatory but the mixture is laevorotatory (inversion of sign)

sub_questions.solution: Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose produced by the acid or enzymatic hydrolysis of sucrose. Sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°), but the resulting mixture of glucose (+52.5°) and fructose (− 92.4°) is laevorotatory overall. Because the sign of optical rotation is inverted (from + to −), the product mixture is called invert sugar.

sub_questions.text: ग्लाइकोसाइडी बंध
sub_questions.text_english: Glycosidic linkage

key_points: Glycosidic linkage is the oxacetal (acetal) bond formed between the anomeric –OH of one monosaccharide unit and the –OH of another, with loss of water

sub_questions.solution: A glycosidic linkage is the covalent bond formed between the anomeric hydroxyl group of one monosaccharide unit and a hydroxyl group of another monosaccharide (or another alcohol), accompanied by the loss of a water molecule. It is essentially an acetal (or ketal) type bond. This linkage joins monosaccharide units together to form disaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides. For example, in sucrose, glucose and fructose are joined by an α-1,β-2 glycosidic linkage.

questions.solution: (a) Anomers are cyclic stereoisomers of a monosaccharide differing only at the anomeric carbon (C-1 for aldoses); α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose are examples. (b) Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose formed by hydrolysis of sucrose; the optical rotation changes sign from dextrorotatory to laevorotatory. (c) Glycosidic linkage is the acetal-type covalent bond formed between the anomeric –OH of one monosaccharide and the –OH of another, with elimination of water.

questions.text:
किसी प्रथम कोटि के तापीय वियघटन अभिक्रिया के लिए निम्न आँकड़े प्राप्त हुए : C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g)
[क्रम संख्या: समय(s), कुल दाब(atm)] [1: 0, 0.30] [2: 30, 0.50]
वेग स्थिरांक की गणना कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained: C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g)
[S.No.: Time(s), Total Pressure(atm)] [1: 0, 0.30] [2: 30, 0.50]
Calculate rate constant. [Given: log 3 = 0.48]

key_points: P₀ = 0.30 atm, P_t = 0.50 atm at t = 30 s
Partial pressure of C₂H₅Cl at time t: P(C₂H₅Cl) = 2P₀ - P_t = 2(0.30) - 0.50 = 0.10 atm

questions.solution: For C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g), let initial pressure P₀ = 0.30 atm. At time t, if x atm of C₂H₅Cl decomposes: total pressure = (0.30 - x) + x + x = 0.30 + x = 0.50 atm, so x = 0.20 atm. Pressure of C₂H₅Cl at t = 30 s: P = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10 atm. For first order reaction: k = (2.303/t) × log(P₀/P) = (2.303/30) × log(0.30/0.10) = (2.303/30) × log 3 = (2.303/30) × 0.48 = 1.1054/30 ≈ 0.0368 s⁻¹. The rate constant k ≈ 3.68 × 10⁻² s⁻¹.
questions.topic: First Order Reaction, Rate Constant from Pressure Data

sub_questions.text: साम्य स्थिरांक (K₀), E°(¹º³ˤ²) से तो संबंधित है, लेकिन E(¹º³ˤ²) से नहीं । क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the Equilibrium Constant (K₇) related to E°₁ₑˡˡ and not to E₁ₑˡˡ ?

key_points: K₇ is related to E°₁ₑˡˡ because at equilibrium E₁ₑˡˡ = 0 and the Nernst equation gives ΔG° = −nFE°₁ₑˡˡ = −RT ln K

sub_questions.solution: The equilibrium constant K₇ is related to E°₁ₑˡˡ (standard emf) because K₇ is defined for standard conditions. The relationship ΔG° = −nFE°₁ₑˡˡ = −RT ln K connects standard emf to the standard free energy change and hence to K. At equilibrium, E₁ₑˡˡ = 0, and the concentrations are non-standard, so using actual E₁ₑˡˡ (which varies with concentration) would not give a constant K. E°₁ₑˡˡ is a fixed value at a given temperature and directly gives the constant K₇.

sub_questions.text: दो धातुओं 'A' और 'B' के मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव क्रमशः –0.24 V और +0.80 V हैं । इनमें से कौन तनु H₂SO₄ से हाइड्रोजन गैस निर्मुक्त करेगी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of –0.24 V and +0.80 V respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. H₂SO₄ ?

key_points: Metal A (E° = –0.24 V) will liberate H₂ because its electrode potential is less than 0 V (H₂/H⁺ potential)

sub_questions.solution: Metal A with E° = –0.24 V will liberate hydrogen gas from dilute H₂SO₄. For a metal to displace hydrogen from an acid, its standard electrode potential must be less than 0 V (i.e., the metal must be more active than hydrogen). Metal A has E° = –0.24 V < 0 V, so it can reduce H⁺ ions to H₂ gas. Metal B has E° = +0.80 V > 0 V, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acid.

sub_questions.text: लेड संचायक बैटरी को आवेशित करते समय होने वाली सेल अभिक्रिया लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the cell reaction which occurs in lead storage battery when it is in charging.

key_points: During charging: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 4H⁺ + 2SO₄²⁻ (reverse of discharge reaction)

sub_questions.solution: During charging of the lead storage battery, external electrical energy drives the reverse of the discharge reaction. The overall cell reaction during charging is: 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l) → Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2SO₄²⁻(aq). At the anode (oxidation): PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → PbO₂ + SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻. At the cathode (reduction): PbSO₄ + 2e⁻ → Pb + SO₄²⁻.

sub_questions.text_english: What type of battery is Mercury cell ? Why it is more advantageous than dry cell ? Write overall reaction taking place in Mercury cell.

key_points: Mercury cell is a primary (non-rechargeable) battery
Advantage: constant voltage output throughout its life unlike dry cell; used in hearing aids, watches
Overall reaction: Zn(Hg) + HgO → ZnO + Hg

sub_questions.solution: Mercury cell is a primary (non-rechargeable) battery. It is more advantageous than a dry cell because it provides a constant voltage of about 1.35 V throughout its useful life, whereas the voltage of a dry cell decreases progressively during use. This makes it suitable for precision instruments such as hearing aids, watches, and cameras. The overall cell reaction in a mercury cell is: Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l). The anode reaction is Zn + 2OH⁻ → ZnO + H₂O + 2e⁻ and the cathode reaction is HgO + H₂O + 2e⁻ → Hg + 2OH⁻.

(ii) Metal A (E° = –0.24 V) will liberate H₂ from dil. H₂SO₄ since its potential is below 0 V. (iii) Charging reaction: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 4H⁺ + 2SO₄²⁻. questions.text: 0.61 g बेन्जोइक अम्ल (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 122 g mol⁻¹) को 5 g CS₂ में घोलने पर, जिसमें यह 88% तक द्वितय बनाता है, बने विलयन का क्वथनांक ज्ञात कीजिए । CS₂ का क्वथनांक और K₇ क्रमशः 46.2 °C और 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ हैं ।
questions.text_english: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing 0.61 g of benzoic acid (Molar mass = 122 g mol⁻¹) in 5 g of CS₂ in which it dimerises to the extent of 88%. The boiling point and K₇ of CS₂ are 46.2 °C and 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.

key_points: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol
Degree of dimerisation α = 0.88; van't Hoff factor i = 1 - α/2 = 1 - 0.44 = 0.56
Boiling point = 46.2 + 1.29 = 47.49 °C

questions.solution: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol. Molality m = 0.005 mol / 0.005 kg = 1 mol kg⁻¹. For dimerisation 2C₆H₅COOH ⇌ (C₆H₅COOH)₂, the van't Hoff factor i = 1 − α/2, where α = 0.88. So i = 1 − 0.88/2 = 1 − 0.44 = 0.56. Elevation in boiling point: ΔT₇ = i × K₇ × m = 0.56 × 2.3 × 1 = 1.288 K ≈ 1.29 K. Boiling point of solution = 46.2 + 1.29 = 47.49 °C.

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनाने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार तथा ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण करता है । क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत (CFT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव (लिगन्डों को बिंदु आवेश मानते हुए उनके द्वारा प्रदत्त प्रभाव) पर आधारित है । प्रबल क्षेत्र तथा दुर्बल क्षेत्र में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं ।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

sub_questions.text: अष्टफलकीय क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र में किन d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा में वृद्धि होती है जब लिगन्ड केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के समीप जाता है ? अपने उत्तर के समर्थन में कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: dᵏ²₋¸² and dᵏ² (eᵍ set) orbitals are raised in energy
These orbitals point directly along the axes towards the ligands, causing greater electrostatic repulsion

sub_questions.solution: In an octahedral crystal field, the energies of the d(z²) and d(x²−y²) orbitals (the eᵍ set) are raised. These two orbitals have their lobes pointing directly along the x, y, and z axes, which are the exact directions from which the six ligands approach the central metal ion. The electrostatic repulsion between the electron density in these orbitals and the lone pairs of the approaching ligands is therefore maximum, destabilising (raising the energy of) these orbitals relative to the average d-orbital energy (barycentre). The other three orbitals (dₓᵧ, dᵧᵦ, dₓᵦ, the t₂ᵍ set) point between the axes and experience less repulsion, so their energy is lowered.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत का उपयोग करके, निम्नलिखित के केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए : (i) [CoF₆]³⁻ (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ [परमाणु क्रमांक : Co = 27]
sub_questions.text_english: Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following: (i) [CoF₆]³⁻ (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ [At. No. : Co = 27]

key_points: Co³⁺ is d⁶; (i) [CoF₆]³⁻: F⁻ is weak field, high spin: t₂ᵍ⁴ eᵍ²; (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: NH₃ is strong field, low spin: t₂ᵍ⁶ eᵍ⁰

sub_questions.solution: Co atomic number is 27, electronic configuration [Ar]3d⁷ 4s². Co³⁺ loses 3 electrons: [Ar]3d⁶, i.e., 6 d-electrons. (i) In [CoF₆]³⁻, F⁻ is a weak field ligand with small crystal field splitting energy Δₒ. The 6 d-electrons occupy orbitals with maximum unpaired electrons (high spin): t₂ᵍ⁴ eᵍ² (4 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic). (ii) In [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, NH₃ is a strong field ligand with large Δₒ (> pairing energy). All 6 electrons pair in the lower t₂ᵍ level (low spin): t₂ᵍ⁶ eᵍ⁰ (0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic).

sub_questions.text: [NiCl₄]²⁻ अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Ni(CO)₄] प्रतिचुंबकीय है यद्यपि दोनों चतुष्फलकीय हैं । क्यों ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)₄] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]

key_points: Ni²⁺ in [NiCl₄]²⁻ (d⁸) with weak field Cl⁻: 2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic; Ni⁰ in [Ni(CO)₄] (d¹⁰) with strong field CO: 0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: In [NiCl₄]²⁻, the central ion is Ni²⁺ (d⁸ configuration). Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand, so the crystal field splitting in the tetrahedral field is small. With 8 d-electrons in the high-spin configuration, there are 2 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic. In [Ni(CO)₄], the central atom is Ni⁰ (d¹⁰ configuration, as CO is a strong field ligand causing 4s electrons to be promoted into 3d). With all 10 d-electrons paired, there are no unpaired electrons, making it diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: संकुल [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ का संकरण एवं चुंबकीय व्यवहार लिखिए । [परमाणु क्रमांक : Fe = 26]
sub_questions.text_english: Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]

key_points: Fe³⁺ is d⁵; CN⁻ is strong field; low spin: d²sp³ hybridisation; 1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic

sub_questions.solution: In [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, the central ion is Fe³⁺. Fe atomic number 26: [Ar]3d⁶ 4s²; Fe³⁺: [Ar]3d⁵. CN⁻ is a strong field ligand. Under the strong field, 4 of the 5 d-electrons pair up in the inner d orbitals, leaving one unpaired electron. The hybridisation is d²sp³ (using two inner 3d orbitals, one 4s, and three 4p orbitals), giving an octahedral geometry. The complex has 1 unpaired electron and is therefore paramagnetic.

questions.text: ऐमीनों की खनिज अम्लों से अभिक्रिया द्वारा अमोनियम लवणों का बनना इनकी क्षारकीय प्रकृति को दर्शाता है । ऐलीफैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया की अपेक्षा प्रबल क्षारक होते हैं जबकि ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया से दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं । ऐलीफैटिक तथा ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक एवं द्वितीयक ऐमीन ऐसिड क्लोराइड, ऐनहाइड्राइड और ऐस्टर से नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया करते हैं । ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन की इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं में मुख्य समस्या इनकी उच्च अभिक्रियाशीलता है । प्रतिस्थापन ऑर्थों तथा पैरा दोनों स्थानों पर हो सकता है । हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक एवं तृतीयक ऐमीनों की पहचान एवं विभेद के लिए प्रयोग में लाया जाता है । प्राय: ऐरिलऐमीन से प्राप्त किये जाने वाले ऐरिलडाइएज़ोनियम लवण, विभिन्न प्रकार के नाभिकरागियों द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किए जाते हैं जिसके द्वारा ऐरिल हेलाइड, सायनाइड, फ़ीनॉल तथा ऐरीन प्राप्त करने की लाभप्रद विधि उपलब्ध होती है ।
questions.text_english: The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

sub_questions.text: जलीय विलयन में (CH₃)₃N की तुलना में CH₃–NH₂ प्रबल क्षारक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why CH₃–NH₂ is a stronger base than (CH₃)₃N in aqueous solution ?

key_points: In aqueous solution (CH₃)₃NH⁺ is sterically hindered and less effectively solvated; CH₃NH₃⁺ is well solvated by water through H-bonding, stabilising the conjugate acid

sub_questions.solution: Although (CH₃)₃N has more electron-donating methyl groups making nitrogen more electron-rich in the gas phase, in aqueous solution CH₃–NH₂ is a stronger base. This is because when CH₃NH₂ is protonated to CH₃NH₃⁺, the three N–H bonds of the cation can form strong hydrogen bonds with water molecules, stabilising the conjugate acid effectively. In contrast, (CH₃)₃NH⁺ has only one N–H bond available for hydrogen bonding with water, and steric hindrance from three methyl groups reduces solvation. This poor solvation of (CH₃)₃NH⁺ makes (CH₃)₃N a weaker base in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: यौगिक A और B के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए : CH₃CONH₂ —NaOBr→ A —C₆H₅COCl/Base→ B
sub_questions.text_english: Write structural formulae of the compound A and B: CH₃CONH₂ —NaOBr→ A —C₆H₅COCl/Base→ B

key_points: A = CH₃NH₂ (methylamine, via Hofmann bromamide reaction)
B = C₆H₅CO–NH–CH₃ (N-methylbenzamide, from acylation of methylamine with benzoyl chloride)

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: CH₃CONH₂ (acetamide) reacts with NaOBr (Hofmann bromamide reaction / Hofmann degradation) to give A = CH₃–NH₂ (methylamine). In this reaction, the amide loses a carbonyl carbon, giving a primary amine with one fewer carbon. Step 2: CH₃–NH₂ (methylamine, A) reacts with C₆H₅COCl (benzoyl chloride) in the presence of base to give B = C₆H₅–CO–NH–CH₃ (N-methylbenzamide) via nucleophilic acyl substitution.

sub_questions.text: C₃H₉N आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X' हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक उत्पाद देता है जो क्षार में अविलेय है । 'X' की पहचान कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: A compound 'X' with molecular formula C₃H₉N reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.

key_points: X is a secondary amine: (CH₃)₂NH (dimethylamine) or CH₃NHCH₂CH₃ (N-methylethylamine)
Product with Hinsberg reagent is insoluble in alkali → secondary amine

sub_questions.solution: Hinsberg reagent (benzenesulfonyl chloride) gives different products with primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. A product insoluble in alkali is characteristic of a secondary amine, because the sulfonamide formed from a secondary amine has no N–H bond and therefore cannot be deprotonated by alkali to form a soluble sodium salt. X has molecular formula C₃H₉N and is a secondary amine. The possible structure is (CH₃)₂NH (dimethylamine) — wait, that is C₂H₇N. For C₃H₉N, it must be N-methylethylamine (CH₃NHCH₂CH₃) or trimethylamine (CH₃)₃N. Since the product is insoluble in alkali (not a tertiary amine which doesn't react), X is CH₃NHCH₂CH₃ (N-methylethylamine, a secondary amine with molecular formula C₃H₉N).

sub_questions.text: आप ऐनिलीन को बेन्जोनाइट्राइल में कैसे रूपांतरित कर सकते हो ?
sub_questions.text_english: How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?

key_points: Aniline → (NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5°C) → benzenediazonium chloride → (CuCN/KCN, Sandmeyer reaction) → benzonitrile

sub_questions.solution: Aniline can be converted to benzonitrile in two steps. First, aniline is treated with NaNO₂ and HCl at 0–5°C (diazotisation) to form benzenediazonium chloride (C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻). Second, the diazonium salt is treated with CuCN (or KCN with Cu catalyst) via the Sandmeyer reaction, replacing the diazonium group (–N₂⁺) with a cyano group (–CN) to give benzonitrile (C₆H₅CN).

sub_questions.text: नाइट्रोकरण करने से पहले ऐनिलीन के –NH₂ समूह का ऐसीटिलन क्यों किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is –NH₂ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?

key_points: To protect the –NH₂ group from getting oxidised by the HNO₃/H₂SO₄ mixture; also to moderate the activating effect and get predominantly para product

sub_questions.solution: The –NH₂ group of aniline is acetylated before nitration for two reasons. First, the free –NH₂ group is easily oxidised by the acidic nitrating mixture (HNO₃ + H₂SO₄), which would destroy the compound. Acetylation converts –NH₂ to –NHCOCH₃ (amide group), which is resistant to oxidation. Second, the amide group is less strongly activating than –NH₂, which moderates the ring's reactivity and gives a better yield of the para-nitro product with less polynitration.

(ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN: Di-tert. butyl ketone, Acetaldehyde, Acetone (iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate. key_points: (a)(i)(I): Methyl ketone, not aldehyde → CH₃CO-CH₂CH₂CH₃ (pentan-2-one) or CH₃CO-CH(CH₃)₂ (3-methylbutan-2-one)
(a)(i)(II): Aldehyde without α-methyl or ketone without CH₃CO group that does aldol: CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO (butanal) + CH₂O not valid; must be C₅H₁₀O ketone without iodoform: pentan-3-one (CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃)
(a)(i)(III): Cannizzaro: no α-H, aldehyde; C₅H₁₀O with no α-H = (CH₃)₃C-CHO (pivaldehyde/2,2-dimethylpropanal)
(a)(ii)(I): Acetophenone + I₂/NaOH (iodoform reaction) or oxidation → benzoic acid
(a)(ii)(II): Ethylbenzene → KMnO₄/H₂SO₄ (oxidation) → benzoic acid
(b)(ii): Di-tert.butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde
(b)(iv): DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride)

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Compound X is C₅H₁₀O. (I) No Tollen’s (not an aldehyde), positive iodoform (has CH₃CO– group): X is a methyl ketone. Structure: pentan-2-one (CH₃–CO–CH₂CH₂CH₃) or 3-methylbutan-2-one (CH₃COCH(CH₃)₂). (II) No Tollen’s, no iodoform (no –CHO and no CH₃CO–), but undergoes aldol (has α-H): Structure is pentan-3-one (CH₃CH₂–CO–CH₂CH₃), a symmetrical ketone with α-H but no methyl ketone group. (III) Cannizzaro reaction (no α-H, is aldehyde): Structure is 2,2-dimethylpropanal [(CH₃)₃C–CHO], the only C₅H₁₀O aldehyde with no α-H.

(a)(ii) (I) Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) can be converted to benzoic acid by the iodoform reaction (I₂/NaOH), giving benzoic acid and CHI₃. (II) Ethylbenzene (C₆H₅CH₂CH₃) is oxidised with acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄, oxidising the alkyl side chain to –COOH, yielding benzoic acid.

(b)(i) 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde: C₆H₅–CH=N–NH–C₆H₃(NO₂)₂ (para and ortho nitro groups at 2 and 4 positions of phenyl ring). (ii) Increasing order of reactivity towards HCN: Di-tert.butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde. Steric bulk reduces reactivity; less electron density on carbonyl carbon reduces nucleophilicity. Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones; bulkier groups further reduce reactivity. (iii) Add NaHCO₃ solution: benzoic acid dissolves with brisk effervescence (CO₂ gas) as it is acidic; ethyl benzoate (ester) does not react with NaHCO₃ and does not dissolve or produce gas. (iv) DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) at −78°C converts ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) to ethanal (CH₃CHO). (v) Cyclohexanol + CrO₃ → X is cyclohexanone (the secondary alcohol is oxidised to a ketone by CrO₃).

(I) Why E°(M²⁺/M) show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why E°(Mn²⁺/Mn) value is highly negative ?

(iii) Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn ?
(iv) What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime ? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called ?

key_points: (a)(i)(I): Irregular trend due to irregular variation in ionisation enthalpies and sublimation enthalpies across the series
(a)(i)(II): Cu has exceptionally high heat of hydration and a filled 3d¹⁰ configuration that resists oxidation, making reduction of Cu²⁺ to Cu favourable
(a)(i)(III): Mn²⁺ has extra stability due to half-filled 3d⁵ configuration; Mn is reluctant to lose electrons, making E° highly negative
(a)(ii) Acidic: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O; Alkaline: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻
(b)(i)(I): Cerium (Ce) shows +4; (II): Europium (Eu) or Ytterbium (Yb) shows +2
(b)(ii): Variable oxidation states allow adsorption and reaction of reactants on surface
(b)(iii): Cr has more unpaired d-electrons available for metallic bonding than Mn (Mn is 3d⁵ 4s², all unpaired in d but d⁵ is half-filled making it stable; Cr is 3d⁵ 4s¹ with more bonding electrons)
(b)(iv): Acidic KMnO₄ standing: auto-oxidation gives MnO₂; disproportionation/auto-oxidation reaction

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(I) The E°(M²⁺/M) values show an irregular trend across the first transition series because these values depend on three energy terms: ionisation enthalpy, sublimation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy. Each of these varies irregularly across the series due to irregular filling of d-orbitals, varying nuclear charge, and varying d-orbital contraction. (II) E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) is exceptionally positive because copper has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ configuration after accepting electrons, which is extra stable. Additionally, Cu has unusually high second ionisation energy and relatively low hydration enthalpy, meaning the overall thermodynamics favours Cu remaining as the metal rather than dissolving as Cu²⁺. This makes the reduction of Cu²⁺ to Cu very favourable and E° positive. (III) E°(Mn²⁺/Mn) is highly negative because Mn²⁺ has the exceptionally stable half-filled d⁵ configuration (all five d-electrons unpaired). The extra stability of Mn²⁺ makes it very reluctant to be reduced back to Mn metal, so Mn metal is very easily oxidised to Mn²⁺, giving a highly negative E°.

(a)(ii) Acidic solution: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O. Alkaline solution: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻.

(b)(i)(I) Cerium (Ce) exhibits the +4 oxidation state (Ce⁴⁺ has a stable empty 4f shell). (II) Europium (Eu) or Ytterbium (Yb) exhibits the +2 oxidation state (stable half-filled or fully filled 4f configurations). (ii) Transition metals act as good catalysts because of their ability to adopt variable oxidation states and to provide active surface sites for the adsorption of reactant molecules. They can form intermediate compounds of variable composition, facilitating the reaction at lower activation energy. (iii) Cr has a higher melting point than Mn because Cr (3d⁵ 4s¹) has a greater number of unpaired electrons available for metallic bonding, while Mn (3d⁵ 4s²) has a half-filled d⁵ configuration which is particularly stable and less available for bonding, resulting in weaker metallic bonds and a lower melting point. (iv) When acidic KMnO₄ solution is allowed to stand for some time, it slowly oxidises itself (auto-catalytic disproportionation): 4KMnO₄ + 2H₂SO₄ → 4MnSO₄ + 2K₂SO₄ + 5O₂ + 2H₂O. Actually the auto-catalytic reaction proceeds as: 4MnO₄⁻ + 4H⁺ → 4MnO₂ + 3O₂ + 2H₂O. This type of reaction is called disproportionation (auto-oxidation-reduction or comproportionation-related decomposition).
